content: 1. Daptomycin is indicated for the treatment of right-sided infective endocarditis caused by methicillin-susceptible and methicillin-resistant isolates. The recommended dosage is 6 mg/kg administered intravenously every 24 hours for a duration of 2 to 6 weeks. However, safety data for use beyond 28 days is limited. In a phase 3 trial, only 14 adults were treated for more than 28 days. 2. Daptomycin is also indicated for the treatment of complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI) caused by susceptible isolates. The recommended dosage is 4 mg/kg administered intravenously every 24 hours for 7 to 14 days. 3. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and maintain the effectiveness of antibacterial drugs, daptomycin should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are proven or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria. 4. The safety and efficacy of daptomycin in children under 1 year of age have not been established. Additionally, dosage regimens for children with renal impairment have not been determined. 5. Co-administration of daptomycin with the cholera vaccine should be avoided or an alternative drug should be used. Systemic antibiotics, including daptomycin, may be active against the vaccine strain, reducing the vaccine's efficacy. Cholera vaccine should not be administered to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 6. Daptomycin may decrease the effects of oral microbiota products due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. These products contain bacterial spores, and co-administration with antibacterial agents may reduce their efficacy. Antibiotic regimens should be completed 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 7. Co-administration of daptomycin with HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g., atorvastatin, fluvastatin, lovastatin, pitavastatin, pravastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin) may increase creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels and the risk of myopathy. Temporary suspension of HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors during daptomycin therapy should be considered. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 8. Daptomycin may decrease the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Caution should be used, and therapy should be monitored. 9. Co-administration of daptomycin with tobramycin may result in decreased tobramycin levels and increased daptomycin levels. The interaction mechanism is unspecified. Therapy should be closely monitored. 10. Serious immune system disorders, including anaphylaxis, hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., angioedema, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms [DRESS], pruritus, hives, shortness of breath, difficulty swallowing, truncal erythema, and pulmonary eosinophilia), have been reported. Systemic steroids may be considered for treatment. 11. Daptomycin use has been associated with Clostridium difficile–associated diarrhea, increased myoglobin levels, rhabdomyolysis, eosinophilic pneumonia, organizing pneumonia, peripheral neuropathy, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, vesiculobullous rash, nausea, vomiting, visual disturbances, anemia, thrombocytopenia, fever, acute kidney injury, renal insufficiency, renal failure, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, epidermal necrolysis, and toxic epidermal necrolysis. 12. Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, may be life-threatening. If an allergic reaction occurs, the drug should be discontinued, and appropriate therapy should be initiated. 13. Daptomycin may cause eosinophilic pneumonia, characterized by fever, cough, shortness of breath, and difficulty breathing. This condition may progress to respiratory failure and can be fatal. Prompt medical evaluation is required, and treatment should be discontinued immediately if symptoms develop. Systemic steroids are recommended for treatment. 14. Prolonged use of daptomycin may result in fungal or bacterial superinfections. Susceptibility testing and evaluation for sequestered foci of infection should be performed if infections persist or relapse. 15. Daptomycin is excreted in breast milk at approximately 1% of the maternal dose. There is no information on its effects on breastfed infants or milk production. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother's clinical need for therapy and potential adverse effects on the infant. 16. Daptomycin is generally considered acceptable during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. 17. There are three formulations of daptomycin with differences in storage and reconstitution requirements. For Cubicin, refrigerate in original packaging at 2–8°C (36–46°F). For Cubicin RF and Dapzura RT, store at controlled room temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Daptomycin 350 mg vials should be refrigerated at 2–8°C (36–46°F) and can be stored at room temperature for up to 12 hours or refrigerated for up to 48 hours after reconstitution.
